title: Noise Injection for Sandbagging Detection: Varying Noise Type and Magnitude

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly tests practical robustness of a proposed sandbagging detection method. If highly sensitive to noise regime, the method's utility is limited and practitioners need to know this before deployment.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires embedding-level noise injection, modifying model inference pipelines, and running prompted sandbagging on coding benchmarks. Token reordering and dropout at embedding level require non-trivial code modifications. Challenging for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined experimental matrix (3 noise types x multiple magnitudes) but the number of runs needed and pipeline complexity could stretch beyond 30 hours. Scoping to 2 noise types would help.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
